# loading  data
library(readr)
## Warning: package 'readr' was built under R version 4.4.2
x <- read_csv("image1.csv")
## Rows: 1000 Columns: 100
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## dbl (100): X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6, X7, X8, X9, X10, X11, X12, X13, X14, X15,...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
x <- data.matrix(x)

# plot to check orientation
plot_image <- function(mat, main = "") {
  image(t(apply(mat, 2, rev)), col = grey(seq(0, 1, length = 256)), 
        axes = FALSE, main = main)
}

# function
rank_k_pca <- function(x, k) {
  pca <- prcomp(x, center = TRUE)
  scores <- pca$x[, 1:k, drop = FALSE]
  loadings <- pca$rotation[, 1:k, drop = FALSE]
  x_approx <- scores %*% t(loadings)
  x_approx <- sweep(x_approx, 2, pca$center, "+")
  error <- sqrt(sum((x - x_approx)^2))
  return(list(approximation = x_approx, error = error))
}

# plot for approximations
approximations <- vector("list", 10)
for (k in 1:10) {
  approximations[[k]] <- rank_k_pca(x, k)$approximation
}
plot_image <- function(mat, main = "", zlim) {
  image(mat, col = grey(seq(0, 1, length = 256)), axes = FALSE, main = main, zlim = zlim)
}


rng <- range(x)  # use original image's range as the common scale

par(mfrow = c(3, 4), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
plot_image(x, main = "Original", zlim = rng)
for (k in 1:10) {
  plot_image(approximations[[k]], main = paste("k =", k), zlim = rng)
}

p <- ncol(x)
n <- nrow(x)
max_k <- min(n, p)

errors <- numeric(max_k)
for (k in 1:max_k) {
  errors[k] <- rank_k_pca(x, k)$error
}

plot(1:max_k, errors, type = "b", pch = 16,
     xlab = "k", ylab = "Frobenius norm error",
     main = "Approximation Error on k")

pca <- prcomp(x, center = TRUE)

first_eigenvector <- pca$rotation[, 1]   # length p (one value per column/pixel-position)
first_pc_score    <- pca$x[, 1]           # length n (one value per row)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(first_eigenvector, type = "l",
     xlab = "Column index (pixel position)", ylab = "Loading",
     main = "First Eigenvector")

plot(first_pc_score, type = "l",
     xlab = "Row index", ylab = "Score",
     main = "First PC Score")

Conclusion

For the first eigenvector the spikes oscillate rapidly between -0.2 and 0.2. This shows what the direction of the strongest variance in this image is and how it spreads across multiple columns creating noise. For the first PC Score it also has a strong spread across 1000 rows. This proves that the pattern from the first eigenvector is distributed evenly. Based on these findings, I think a k of 60/100 will show more of the original texture with more variance as well. We can compare it below

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot_image(x, main = "Original Image", zlim = rng)
plot_image(rank_k_pca(x, 60)$approximation, main = "k=60", zlim = rng)
